story.what_it_does: Sarda Energy & Minerals is an integrated steel, ferro alloy, mining and power group. Power now supplies about two-thirds of EBITDA (over 75% in H1 FY27), with coal mines, pellets and steel alongside. In FY25-26 consolidated revenue was ₹5,690 crore and profit ₹1,103 crore.
story.plans: Management wants to double energy capacity to 1,200 MW and double EBITDA by FY30, and to expand pellets from 0.9 to 2.0 million tonnes. It also plans a 50 MW captive solar plant, new coal mines (Shahpur West, Bartunga Hill) and a manganese mine. Capex guidance is ₹500-700 crore a year, excluding thermal expansion that still needs approvals.
story.moat: The notes point to owned power, coal mining and pellet assets that supply its own steel and ferro alloy plants. The Rehar hydro plant has a 40-year power agreement at ₹7.42 per unit, and two new power purchase agreements add revenue visibility. The notes do not describe any competitive advantage beyond this, and steel and power prices are cyclical.

scenarios.story: Net debt is now negative and liquidity is about ₹2,500 crore, which funds the expansion plans. If the solar plant, new mines and 1,200 MW thermal capacity arrive on time, EBITDA could double as targeted.
signals_to_watch: Commissioning of the 50 MW captive solar plant and Shahpur West coal mine
Return to a normal operating trajectory after shutdowns from Q2 FY27 onward

scenarios.story: Power keeps earnings steady while steel and ferro alloy output is hit by planned shutdowns, and H1 FY27 EBITDA was a record but up only 4%. Management gives no FY27 guidance, so results depend on metal and power prices.
signals_to_watch: Steel and ferro alloy price direction given the West Asia situation
Power realisation per unit against the expected ₹5 or more

scenarios.story: Underlying profit is weaker than headlines because one-time benefits (₹110 crore in Q1, ₹15 crore in Q2) helped, and steel volumes fell sharply. Pending approvals, the disputed ₹127 crore cess at the Supreme Court and higher input costs could delay growth or hurt earnings.
